newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt parties to meet 1800 GMT on DPEF.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt parties to meet 1800 GMT on DPEF.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi will meet leaders of parties in his centre-left coalition at 1800 GMT on Monday to discuss his government's proposed rolling three-year economic strategy, political sources said.

The strategy, known as the economic and financial planning document (DPEF), is due to be approved by the cabinet on Friday and will outline how the government intends to cut another 25 trillion lire ($15 billion) from the public deficit in the 1988 budget.
The DPEF is a crucial part of Italy's plans for stabilising state finances and keeping alive hopes of joining a European currency union by the planned 1999 start date.
Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi said on Friday that the government was still debating what the exact mix should be between spending cuts and fresh revenue-raising measures.

Italian newspapers have reported that the government plans to reduce spending by 17 trillion lire -- including eight trillion lire in social security and welfare spending cuts -- and to raise eight trillion lire in increased revenues.
Prodi is expected to spell out details of the strategy to business and trades union leaders at meetings on Thursday.

The loudest opposition to cuts in social spending comes from Fausto Bertinotti, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation Party. The government depends for its survival in the lower house of parliament on support from Refoundation.
Bertinotti has said he accepts the idea of shaking up an outmoded welfare state but opposes wholesale cuts.
